title: Rung two, one-hot-off dirt: if no least AND/OR fan-in-two 4-cycle-free bipartite edge circuit has one dirty AND, none with one-hot-off dirt has two
statement:
(∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (s : Fin n → Bool),
  (∀ u v : Fin n, G.Adj u v → s u ≠ s v) → PEqualNP.TopForm.NoFourCycle G → PEqualNP.TopForm.IsLeastAO G C →
  (PEqualNP.TopForm.junk G C).card ≠ 1) →
∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (s : Fin n → Bool),
  (∀ u v : Fin n, G.Adj u v → s u ≠ s v) → PEqualNP.TopForm.NoFourCycle G → PEqualNP.TopForm.IsLeastAO G C →
  (∀ k ∈ PEqualNP.TopForm.junk G C, ∀ v : Fin n, PEqualNP.EdgeOwnership.gateVal n C k (PEqualNP.SplitCount.unitInput v) = false) →
  (PEqualNP.TopForm.junk G C).card ≠ 2
unlocks: the half of the second rung whose argued cases are on paper: both misbehaving ANDs off at one-hot inputs
context: SKETCH: No proof is in hand. Take the first rung as the hypothesis it is. Both ANDs not below F are off at one-hot inputs, so each is OR(A) AND OR(B), A and B disjoint. A case split written in house (it builds; it is not a checked row) reduces this to ten case statements that partition the possibilities; paper arguments cover parts of them (small rectangles, the five-vertex path core by a star swap) and leave named gaps: two flags with no overlap, rectangles beyond two by two, factors with variables on both sides. Size: open. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
